name: AlphaGeometry2
one_liner: A stronger AlphaGeometry: a Gemini-based model proposes constructions, several search trees share what they learn, and a symbolic engine checks the proof.

loop.proposes: Auxiliary constructions for geometry problems, from a Gemini-architecture language model
loop.steers: Parallel search trees share facts (SKEST), so one tree's findings guide the others

headline_result: Solves 42 of 50 IMO geometry problems from 2000 to 2024 (IMO-AG-50); the paper states an overall solving rate of 84% on geometry problems from the last 25 years versus 54% for the original, and says AG2 surpasses an average gold medalist. The formal language now covers 88% of those problems, up from 66%.
caveat: Geometry only. The paper reports progress toward, not completion of, a fully automated pipeline from natural-language problem statements. The AG2 system was also part of the IMO 2024 silver-medal-standard result.
beyond_harness_note: Same symbolic-engine-in-charge design as the original, now with a population of search trees that exchange knowledge.
generative_model: Gemini-architecture language model trained on synthetic data

sources.title: Gold-medalist Performance in Solving Olympiad Geometry with AlphaGeometry2

verification.notes: Read the arXiv abstract and the PDF text (section stating '42 out of 50 of all 2000-2024 IMO geometry problems'; SKEST named in the contributions). Report claim of 'above average gold-medalist' matches the abstract wording. Set parent=alphageometry.
